reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disorder caused by variants in ALDOB, encoding aldolase B, the liver, kidney and intestinal isoform of fructose-1-phosphate aldolase
Symptoms begin when fructose, sucrose or sorbitol is introduced into the diet, classically at weaning
Acute ingestion causes hypoglycaemia, vomiting, sweating, tremor and, if severe, seizures and shock
Chronic exposure produces failure to thrive, hepatomegaly, jaundice, coagulopathy and progressive liver and renal (proximal tubular) dysfunction
Affected individuals characteristically develop a strong aversion to sweet foods, which can be protective

The biochemical mechanism is accumulation of fructose-1-phosphate, which traps inorganic phosphate and inhibits glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, producing hypoglycaemia and a Fanconi-like renal tubulopathy
Diagnosis is confirmed by ALDOB genetic testing, avoiding the older and hazardous fructose tolerance test
Management is lifelong dietary exclusion of fructose, sucrose and sorbitol, which allows normal growth and reverses organ dysfunction
reference.pathophysiology: Aldolase B cleaves fructose-1-phosphate during hepatic fructose metabolism. When the enzyme is deficient, fructose-1-phosphate accumulates rapidly in the liver, kidney and intestine after fructose ingestion. This accumulation sequesters inorganic phosphate, depleting the free phosphate and ATP needed for other metabolic processes, and it inhibits both glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis, producing acute hypoglycaemia. The intracellular phosphate depletion and metabolite accumulation also impair hepatocyte and renal tubular function, causing liver injury, coagulopathy and a proximal renal tubular acidosis. Removing dietary fructose prevents metabolite accumulation and allows recovery.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of ketotic and non-ketotic hypoglycaemia in infancy
Glycogen storage disorders with hypoglycaemia and hepatomegaly
Neonatal or infantile hepatitis and other causes of liver failure
Renal tubular acidosis of other causes
additionalInvestigations: Molecular genetic testing of ALDOB (preferred confirmatory test)
Blood glucose, liver function tests and coagulation studies during exposure
Assessment of renal tubular function for a Fanconi-like picture
Urinalysis for reducing substances (fructosuria) after fructose ingestion
Liver imaging or biopsy where hepatic disease is unexplained
Dietary history correlating symptoms with fructose-containing foods
redFlags: Acute hypoglycaemia and vomiting after introducing fruit, sucrose or sorbitol
Progressive liver dysfunction with coagulopathy in an infant
Renal tubular dysfunction of unclear cause
Severe reaction to intravenous fluids or medicines containing fructose or sorbitol
reference.prognosis: With strict lifelong exclusion of fructose, sucrose and sorbitol the prognosis is excellent, and hepatic and renal abnormalities typically resolve. Continued exposure, or delayed diagnosis, can cause progressive liver failure, renal damage and, in acute crises, death.
pitfalls: Performing an intravenous fructose tolerance test, which can precipitate dangerous hypoglycaemia and should be avoided
Overlooking fructose or sorbitol content of intravenous fluids and medicines
Attributing the hepatopathy or tubulopathy to other causes and missing the dietary trigger
Assuming a normal appearance excludes disease before fructose is introduced into the diet
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease
management: Strict lifelong dietary exclusion of fructose, sucrose and sorbitol is the definitive treatment and reverses the metabolic abnormalities
Emergency treatment of acute ingestion with intravenous glucose to correct hypoglycaemia, alongside supportive care for vomiting and shock
Supplement vitamin C and other micronutrients that may be deficient on a fructose-restricted diet, under dietitian oversight
Screen all medicines and excipients for hidden fructose or sorbitol content and avoid them, including sorbitol-containing intravenous fluids
Monitor liver function, coagulation, growth and renal proximal tubular (Fanconi-like) function
Genetic counselling and family testing for ALDOB variants
Provide alert documentation warning against intravenous fructose- or sorbitol-containing infusions
